text:
lucas_fin: Noticed an unexpected GCP Marketplace adjustment on invoice INV-GCP-2026-06 for reseller SummitEdge (reseller_id SE-304). There's a duplicated partner fee line resulting in an extra $3,112. Can someone pull the full line items?

maya_ops: pulling the export now. will paste the snippet.

jon_sales: SummitEdge reported a billing mismatch yesterday; they thought they'd been credited not debited. we held off responding.

maya_ops: CSV snippet from GCP billing export:
```
invoice_id,sku,description,units,unit_price,total
INV-GCP-2026-06,MP-RESELLER-02,Redwood Inference - tokens gen,1800000,0.072,129600.00
INV-GCP-2026-06,MP-RESELLER-02,Partner Service Fee,1,0.00,-3112.00
INV-GCP-2026-06,MP-RESELLER-02,Partner Service Fee,1,0.00,-3112.00
```

lucas_fin: two identical Partner Service Fee lines. looks like a duplicate credit applied twice (reducing our revenue twice). need to know if GCP sent an amended credit or if our reconciliation pipeline duplicated the line.

anya_rev: tagging REV-5117. I saved the raw export and will run our dedupe check. If it is a duplicate on GCP side, we'll request corrected invoice. If duplication occurred in our pipeline we need to reverse the extra credit and correct rev-rec for June.

gcp-billing-bot: Support case opened: CASE-GCP-889201. Subject: "Duplicate partner fee lines on INV-GCP-2026-06 for SE-304". GCP ETA: 3 business days.

maya_ops: i've checked our ingestion logs for the month and the billing message from GCP only contained two fee lines; our dedupe logic would have collapsed identical line_ids but these lines have different line_id hashes. forwarding the exact payload to CASE-GCP-889201.

jon_sales: SummitEdge wants a statement they can give to their finance team. If GCP won't clarify quickly, we may need to issue a temporary partner statement acknowledging investigation.

lucas_fin: don't issue external statements that imply liability. We can provide a neutral "investigation in progress" note. Also need to estimate P&L impact for Q2 close: if both credits stand we lose $6,224 in net revenue; commissions and accruals affected.

anya_rev: preliminary rev impact calc: net revenue delta $6,224, expected commission clawback exposure ~$747 at 12%. Flagged REV-5117 with estimates and uploaded to the month-end folder.

gcp-billing-bot: CASE-GCP-889201 updated: GCP requested line item manifests and partner entitlement mapping.

maya_ops: GCP replied: one line was an "initial partner fee" and the second was an "automated reconciliation credit" referencing a prior month. They claim both are valid but will provide manifests. Asking us to confirm mapping to reseller SE-304.

lucas_fin: if GCP shows manifest proving both credits are legitimate, we need to reconcile with SummitEdge and either absorb or charge back per contract. What does contract say about automated reconciliations?

jon_sales: contract clause 4.2 says marketplace-level reconciliations can be passed through to partner unless they're due to provider error. We need to verify whether the reconciliation credit corresponds to an earlier overcharge to SummitEdge. If so, they should keep the credit. If not, we may need to reverse.

anya_rev: Requested manifests mapped to our internal billing IDs. Also asked GCP for timestamped audit trail and the original charge they say was corrected.

gcp-billing-bot: CASE-GCP-889201: manifest files uploaded by GCP.

maya_ops: received manifest — looks like the reconciliation credit references usage from Apr-2026 that was originally billed to a different reseller tag, then re-attributed to SE-304 in a consolidation pass. GCP's note: "re-attribution due to partner entitlement normalization".

lucas_fin: so GCP re-attributed historical usage to SummitEdge and then applied a reconciliation credit. That explains their side, but we need to know whether our original payouts to SummitEdge already accounted for that usage.

anya_rev: checking payout ledger now. our payout to SE-304 for Apr had no such extra credit. It appears we already paid the commission on the original charge. If GCP's credit stands, we will need to recover commission overpayment or negotiate with SummitEdge.

jon_sales: I'll reach out to SummitEdge (cc finance) with a neutral summary: GCP re-attributed some historical usage and applied a credit; we're verifying impact and will follow up with a reconciliation statement. Keep the language factual.

lucas_fin: agree. also prepare two internal paths: A) GCP issues corrected invoice reversing the duplicate credit -> we reverse our adjustments and close. B) GCP insists both credits are valid -> we prepare a chargeback/commission clawback plan and legal review.

maya_ops: setting internal ticket OPS-7654 to implement automated flag if manifest attribution changes for resellers.

gcp-billing-bot: CASE-GCP-889201 closed: GCP confirmed both credits are valid and provided line-level evidence.

anya_rev: with GCP confirmation, we need to proceed with partner reconciliation. Drafting commission reclaim calc and partner notification for Jon to review.

jon_sales: thanks. i'll draft the partner note and coordinate with legal if they dispute.

lucas_fin: for audit, keep this thread as canonical. mark SE-304 partner record as "billing_adjusted_q2_2026". We will book the $6,224 variance and the expected commission clawback for Q2.

maya_ops: noted. OPS-7654 updated and REV-5117 closed with attachments.

jon_sales: sending the neutral partner note now.

lucas_fin: closing this thread. thanks everyone for quick turnaround.
